en: Put your trust in grown-ups carelessly,
and nothing good ever comes of it!
Damn it, it pisses me off.
Every last one of them, for selfish reasons,
keeps yanking me around.
They all put on a saintly face,
then betray people right to their faces.
My old man, the kids at school, all of them.
Why are you so
eager to trust everyone?
"Eager to trust"?
Me
Trusting everyone
You're kind, Ludwig.
I never try to trust anyone to begin with,
so being "betrayed" can't even happen to me.
(Me, "eager to trust"?)
To me, you seem like a pretty kind person.
But you "don't try to trust" anyone,
you said.
note: quote moved to #498; 'you said.' stays in its own row

en: Doesn't that kind of contradict itself?
Maybe so.
In my case
I suppose I "choose" who and what to trust.
Trusting every adult you mean, Ludwig,
note: restructured: 'Trusting ... is something I just can't do' so #505 keeps the verb

en: is something I just can't do.
To "choose" who and what to trust
Oh, time's up.
You can head home,

note: Ludwig mocking 'sa-n' suffix; reduced to the closing '.' after the name

en: I'm still not going to school.
Being around those ugly adults
is still something I hate, it seems.
Maybe watching the people who gather around my old man
made me this way.
Would you mind if I read
this book too?
Ah,
note: Shared: Ludwig 'Ah, sure.', Lord Stanberg 'Ah, <name>...' (needs #4690 to continue after the name); Zille answers 'A farm?' so variants give 'Yes.'

en: go ahead.
Reading a book slowly in my room like this
calms me down.
Even the adults who staged ugly fights before my eyes,
I feel like I could forgive them.
I wonder why they were chasing
after such petty things. All of them.
Anything you say, I'll
do it
note: completes #525 'Anything you say, I'll' + 'do it'; followed by #2 + #25 (msg 21131)

en: do it...
note: completes #525; contains its own ellipsis, followed by #25 (msg 21170)

en: You're wearing some pretty odd clothes, huh.
Whoa, don't follow me.
A flashy guy like you with me stands out,
note: shared by msgs 21206, 21935, 21247; must be completed by #531 or #534 ('and that's a pain.')

en: and that's a pain.
Please, whatever you do, don't tail me,
okay
and that's a pain.
And whatever you do, don't follow me, okay?
Man, I just can't make up my mind.
I don't want to worry my sister any more.
Quitting that cargo-pilfering business for good
was the right call.
That sort of work was never really
my kind of thing anyway.
I'm on my way home right now.
See ya.
note: shared with Hermann (msgs 103333, 103873): 'See ya.' works for both

en: Man, you sure do wear flashy clothes.
Who are you, anyway?
Are you, like, super rich or something?
My sister must be worried.
The doctor told her to stay in bed, but
she's out looking for me anyway.
I quit a shady job like pilfering cargo,
and it feels great.
My sister seems relieved too.
I'm Anton. It's just me and my sister.
I got fired from the factory, so I'm out of
work right now
note: completes #554 'I'm out of' + 'work right now'; followed by #2 + #25

en: Ah. What am I supposed to do?
I know it's shady work, but
I need the money, no matter what
I'm agonizing over this
